simple: a picture that says: write many small, fast tests, fewer tests that join parts together, and only a few tests of the whole system.
analogy: check every brick, many joints, and walk through the finished house a few times.
precise: a heuristic for the shape of a test portfolio, with test levels ordered by scope; the narrow, cheap, precise levels at the wide base and the broad, slow, ambiguous levels at the narrow top. It is a starting shape, not a law.
source: D1 of F12-06, D3 of F12-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: a test that runs two or more real parts together and checks that they agree.
analogy: checking the joint between the wall and the window frame.
precise: a test whose scope covers the interface between units (data formats, units of measure, call order, error conventions) with the real implementations on both sides, in contrast to a unit test, which isolates one unit.
source: D5 of F12-06, R1 of F12-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: a test of the whole thing doing its job, judged by what a user would see.
analogy: walking through the finished house in the rain.
precise: a test that exercises the complete system (here, the closed control loop with a simulated world) against its requirements, observing only externally visible behaviour.
source: D5 of F12-06, R1 of F12-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: the rule that decides whether a result is right.
analogy: the drawing the inspector compares the wall with.
precise: the mechanism that judges an observed outcome as pass or fail: an expected value, a requirement such as "never closer than 0.35 m", a reference model, or a property; in curriculum section 0 the oracle for kernel tests is the serial output.
source: D2 of F12-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: a stand-in for a real part, used only in tests.
analogy: a wooden frame standing in for the window while the wall is built.
precise: an object or function that replaces a real dependency in a test; kinds include fakes (a working light implementation), stubs (fixed answers) and mocks (which also check how they were called). In this chapter the simulated world is a test double for the real corridor. Not to be confused with the RPC stub of F5-09, which is production code.
source: D1 of F12-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: a test both sides of an interface agree on, so neither can change the deal alone.
analogy: one shared drawing of the window opening, signed by the bricklayers and the window maker.
precise: a test that checks a property of an interface (here: "the parser returns metres") and is run against every implementation and by every consumer of that interface.
source: D1 of F12-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: a test that brings everything it needs and touches nothing outside itself.
analogy: testing a door in the workshop, not in a house where people walk through it.
precise: a test that depends only on inputs it controls (no network, shared files, real clock or shared state), so its result depends only on the code under test.
source: D1 of F12-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: the control code built for the robot's own kind of processor, still driving a simulated robot.
analogy: the real controller's chip on a bench, wired to the rig, but not yet in its box.
precise: a closed-loop test in which the controller is compiled with the target's compiler for the target's instruction set and executed on that processor (or, as in this chapter, on an emulator of it), while the plant remains simulated; it checks compilation, numerics and the interface, not real-time behaviour.
source: D1 of F12-07, R5 of F12-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: how much of the real world the simulator includes, and how accurately.
analogy: whether the rig's thermometer is slow like the real one.
precise: the set of physical effects a simulation models (dynamics, delays, noise, saturation, quantisation, failures) and the accuracy of their parameters; a test result is only valid for the effects modelled. Fidelity is chosen per question: more is not always better if it costs speed or determinism.
source: D2 of F12-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: the same test run in many versions of the world, one for every combination of the things that may differ.
analogy: testing the boiler with cold and mild weather, open and closed windows, slow and fast thermometers.
precise: a set of system-test runs over the cross product of chosen world parameters (here latency × noise × start distance), each judged against the requirements, so the boundary of safe operation becomes visible.
source: R1 of F12-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: testing the real robot in the real place where it will work, with people watching.
analogy: the first winter morning in the finished house.
precise: a supervised test of the complete physical system in its operating environment; it produces evidence nothing else can, at the highest cost and risk, and therefore comes last, after simulation and bench tests pass (BR-08).
source: D2 of F12-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: instead of checking a few chosen examples, you write a rule that must hold for every input, and the computer tries many random inputs.
analogy: "every door closes", tried on many doors.
precise: a testing method in which a property (a predicate over inputs and outputs) is checked on many inputs produced by a generator; a failing input is reported together with the seed that reproduces it, and is usually shrunk. Popularised by the QuickCheck library for Haskell.
source: D1 of F12-08, R1 of F12-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: the part that invents test inputs.
analogy: Lina's way of choosing which door to try next and how wide to open it.
precise: a function from a pseudo-random source and a size parameter to an input value; its distribution decides which inputs are likely, and therefore which bugs can be found. Not the CMake generator of F2-26.
source: D1 of F12-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: making a failing input smaller and smaller while it still fails.
analogy: pushing the door less and less wide until the smallest failing push is found.
precise: after a property fails, repeatedly replacing the failing input by a "smaller" candidate (fewer elements, smaller values) that still fails, until no candidate fails; the result is a local minimum, not necessarily the smallest failing input.
source: D1 of F12-08, R1 of F12-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: comparing your clever code with a simple version that is obviously right.
analogy: checking the automatic door against a plain hinged door that does the same job.
precise: a property of the form "for every sequence of operations, the system under test returns the same results as a reference model"; here a ring buffer against std::deque. Related to the reference model of F1-14.
source: D1 of F12-08, R2 of F12-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: if you pack something and unpack it, you get back what you started with.
analogy: taking a door off its hinges and putting it back: it must close as before.
precise: for an encoder e and decoder d, d(e(x)) = x for every valid x; one of the most productive properties for parsers, serialisers and compressors.
source: D1 of F12-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: the list of checks a computer runs, in order, on every change before the change is accepted.
analogy: the inspector's evening round: pipes first, then wiring, then stairs.
precise: an ordered set of stages (build, tests, analyses) run automatically for each commit or merge request; each stage has a pass, fail or skipped result, a failing stage stops the pipeline, and the overall result gates the merge.
source: D1 of F12-09, R1 of F12-09 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: a pretend device in QEMU that a kernel can write a number to, which makes QEMU stop with an exit status.
analogy: the plumber flips a green or red card that the inspector can read from the road.
precise: a QEMU device on the ISA I/O port bus (here at port 0xf4); a write of value v ends the emulator with exit status (v << 1) | 1, as observed in this build (0x10 gave 33, 0x11 gave 35); the status is therefore always odd, and the harness must map one chosen value to "pass".
source: D2 of F12-09, D3 of F12-09, R2 of F12-09 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: the most time a test may take; if it takes longer, it has failed.
analogy: the inspector does not wait all night for a pressure test to finish.
precise: a limit on real elapsed time enforced from outside the test (here by timeout, exit status 124 when it fires); the curriculum's rule: "a hang is a failure, not 'probably fine'".
source: D2 of F12-09, R1 of F12-09 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: a test that is supposed to fail, run to prove that the harness notices failures.
analogy: the inspector checks her gauge on a pipe with a known leak.
precise: a deliberately failing case (panic, hang, no tests run) executed through the real harness in CI, with the stage passing only if every such case is reported as a failure; it protects the oracle itself from regressions. Related to mutation testing.
source: R1 of F12-09 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: "this check did not run here", reported as its own result, never as a pass.
analogy: "lift not inspected: lift engineer absent", written in the site book in red.
precise: a third verdict next to pass and fail, for tests whose preconditions (a GPU, a robot rig) are absent; the pipeline's summary names every skipped stage so that missing evidence stays visible, and a policy decides where the skipped test must still run before release.
source: D2 of F12-09, R1 of F12-09 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: a shell setting that makes a chain of commands joined by | fail if any command in the chain fails.
analogy: the report says "fail" if any trade failed, not only the last one to sign.
precise: in bash, set -o pipefail makes the exit status of a pipeline the status of the last command that failed (or 0 if all succeeded); without it the status is that of the last command only, so qemu ... | tee log reports tee's success.
source: D4 of F12-09, R6 of F12-09 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: how often a flaky test fails on code that has not changed.
analogy: how many false beeps the alarm gives per week.
precise: the estimated probability p that one run of a test fails, measured as failures ÷ runs over repeated runs of one fixed commit in one fixed environment; it depends on the machine and its load, so it is recorded together with them.
source: D2 of F12-10, R1 of F12-10 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: running the same test many times on the same code to see whether it ever fails.
analogy: lighting a candle under the alarm a hundred times to see whether it always beeps.
precise: executing a test n times on one commit, often with load, shuffled order or different CPU counts, to estimate its flake rate or to gain confidence in a fix; the number of runs follows from the rate you want to detect (worked example).
source: R2 of F12-10 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: a test whose result depends on which tests ran before it.
analogy: an alarm that only works if the alarm next door was tested first.
precise: a test that reads state another test leaves behind (globals, caches, files, a database, environment variables), so it passes or fails depending on the execution order; a failure of test isolation. Shuffling the order with a printed seed exposes it.
source: D2 of F12-10, R1 of F12-10 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: when a test fails, run it again and accept the result if it passes the second time.
analogy: when the alarm beeps, wait to see if it beeps again before leaving.
precise: a CI policy that re-executes failing tests and reports a pass if a retry passes; it hides a failure of probability p with probability about 1 − p, so it hides real intermittent bugs as well as test defects, and must be recorded and counted when used at all.
source: D1 of F12-10, R5 of F12-10 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: moving a flaky test out of the blocking suite while it is fixed, with a name, an owner and a date.
analogy: taping a note on the alarm "under repair, fire warden checks room 14 by hand until Friday".
precise: a recorded exclusion of a known-flaky test from the merge gate; it keeps running and reporting outside the gate, has an owner and a deadline, and returns to the gate only after a repeat run shows the fix. For curriculum acceptance tests it is a weakening and needs the learner's approval.
source: D1 of F12-10, D3 of F12-10 (R = lab run in this build; D = book, manual or curriculum cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)
